title: XXII-XXV: approving, efficient, and permitting will
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Acts 4:28. though He hates it, He does not impede because belonging toward a joined good — so God willed to permit ye fall belonging toward ye first parents, Romans 9:17; — permitting stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which He wills something to happen which. XXV. plus to work something in or through something — efficient stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God wills to produce something. XXIV. that same which yet He does not effect — approving stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God loves something as a possible good not dissonant out from His nature. XXIII. Others distinguish in ye same sense into ye will belonging toward approbation plus belonging toward decree. FIFTH, God's will stands as approving, or efficient, or permitting. XXII.
pass_b_english: XXII. FIFTH, God's will is approving, or efficient, or permitting. Others distinguish in the same sense into the will of approbation and of decree. XXIII. Approving is that by which God loves something as a possible good not dissonant from His nature, which yet He does not effect. XXIV. Efficient is that by which God wills to produce something, and to work something in or through something. XXV. Permitting is that by which He wills something to happen which, though He hates it, He does not impede because of a joined good — so God willed to permit the fall of the first parents, Romans 9:17; Acts 4:28.
source_text: XXII. QUINTO, voluntas Dei est approbans, aut efficiens, aut permittens. Alii distinguunt eodem sensu in voluntatem approbationis et decreti. XXIII. Approbans est qua Deus aliquid amat tanquam bonum possibile a natura sua haud dissentaneum, quod tamen non efficiat. XXIV. Efficiens est qua Deus vult aliquid producere, et aliquid in aliquo aut per aliquid operari. XXV. Permittens est qua aliquid fieri vult, quamvis oderit, propter bonum conjunctum, non impedire — sic Deus lapsum primorum parentum permittere voluit, Rom. IX.17; Act. IV.28.
